candidates: Use a consistent TypeScript typing style for Vue reactive refs throughout a file — don't mix `const x: Ref<T> = ref(value)` with `const x = ref<T>(value)` in the same component.

Don't initialize a reactive `ref` (or any variable) with a value outside a lifecycle hook if that value is unconditionally overwritten inside the hook before it is ever read; the initial assignment is dead code and should be removed.

Don't use optional chaining (`?.`) or optional type markers (`?`) on values that are already guaranteed to be non-nullish by the surrounding logic or TypeScript types; unnecessary optionality obscures intent and can suppress real type errors.
